commands.author: zhangqueping

target.title: fix(memory-wiki): strip fenced code and inline code before wikilink extraction
target.body:
## Summary

**Problem**: `extractWikiLinks` in `extensions/memory-wiki/src/markdown.ts` runs wikilink regexes against full markdown including fenced code blocks and inline code, causing false-positive `broken-wikilink` warnings from `[[...]]` syntax in code (bash test expressions, Scala/C# generics).

**Solution**: Replace the lazy regex/callback fenced-code stripper with a line-by-line scanner that handles backtick and tilde fences, CommonMark longer-close behavior, and invalid fence-looking lines inside longer blocks. Rebased onto main which already has PR #97954's basic backtick-fence stripping via backreference.

**What changed**: `extensions/memory-wiki/src/markdown.ts` — replace `FENCED_CODE_BLOCK_RE` regex/callback with `stripFencedCodeBlocks()` line scanner (+38/-12), export `extractWikiLinks`. `extensions/memory-wiki/src/markdown.test.ts` — add scanner-specific regression test for shorter fence lines inside longer blocks (+18 lines). Total +56/-12 in 2 source files.

**What did NOT change**: `RELATED_BLOCK_PATTERN`, `OBSIDIAN_LINK_PATTERN`, `MARKDOWN_LINK_PATTERN`, link target normalization, frontmatter handling. Indented code blocks (4-space) still not stripped.

Fixes #97945

## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw wiki lint` produces false-positive `broken-wikilink` warnings from `[[...]]` inside tilde-fenced code blocks and longer fenced blocks with shorter interior fence-like lines. Both cases are not covered by main's current `\2` backreference regex:

- Tilde fences (`~~~scala\nFuture[Option[User]]\n~~~`) — main only strips backtick fences
- Shorter fence lines inside longer blocks — main's lazy regex stops at the first close candidate

## Root Cause

Main's `extractWikiLinks` (from PR #97954) strips fenced code with `/(^|\n)(`{3,})[^\n]*\n[\s\S]*?\n\2(?=\n|$)/g` which:
1. Requires closing fence to match exactly (`\2` backreference) — tilde fences, longer closes not handled
2. Uses lazy quantifier (`[\s\S]*?`) — stops at first close candidate, leaks wikilinks past invalid interior fence lines

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed**: `openclaw wiki lint` produces false-positive `broken-wikilink` warnings from `[[...]]` patterns inside tilde-fenced code blocks and longer fenced blocks with invalid interior fence lines

**Real environment tested**: Node 24.13.1, Linux x86_64, `npx tsx` direct import of production `extractWikiLinks` from PR head markdown.ts

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**: `npx tsx /tmp/memory-wiki-proof/extract-links-proof.mjs` importing production `extractWikiLinks` directly, testing 5 scenarios (backtick fence, tilde fence, inline code, longer closing fence, shorter fence line inside longer block)

**After-fix evidence**:
```
======================================================================
  extractWikiLinks – L2 Proof (real function + real data)
======================================================================
  ✓ bash test [[...]] inside fenced code block
    → links: ["RealPage"]
  ✓ Scala generic inside tilde-fenced code block
    → links: ["TargetPage"]
  ✓ shorter fence-like line inside longer fenced block (scanner P2)
    → links: ["AfterFence"]
  ✓ inline code [[...]] excluded
    → links: ["RealPage"]
  ✓ real broken link still reports in prose
    → links: ["MissingPage"]

  5/5 passed, 0 failed
======================================================================
```

**Observed result after the fix**: All false positives from fenced code blocks (backtick, tilde, varying lengths) and inline code spans are eliminated. Real wikilinks in prose continue to be extracted correctly. The scanner correctly skips past invalid interior fence-like lines.

**What was not tested**: Live vault with production Obsidian render mode and thousands of pages (requires real production vault). Same approach validated in #70986 on a production vault (warnings dropped from 70 to 4).

## Evidence

### L2 Proof — Direct function import

The 5 scenarios exercised by direct `npx tsx` import:

| # | Scenario | Fence Type | Verified |
|---|----------|-----------|----------|
| 1 | Bash `[[ "$name" == "Alice" ]]` in ```bash block | Backtick-fenced | Not extracted |
| 2 | Scala `Future[Option[User]]` in ~~~scala block | Tilde-fenced | Not extracted |
| 3 | Shorter ``` inside longer `````` block (P2 fix) | Mixed-length | Not extracted |
| 4 | `` `[[ -z "$str" ]]` `` inline code | Inline backtick | Not extracted |
| 5 | Prose `[[RealPage]]` outside code | None | Extracted correctly |

### Unit Tests

```
pnpm test extensions/memory-wiki/src/markdown.test.ts extensions/memory-wiki/src/lint.test.ts
 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  29 passed (29)  (18 markdown + 11 lint)
```

New test: "does not leak [[…]] when a shorter fence-like line appears inside a longer fenced block" — exercises the scanner P2 fix.

## Risk checklist

**Highest-risk area**: False-positive strip of a real wikilink inside a region that accidentally matches a fenced code open/close pattern on its own line. Mitigated by requiring 0-3 space indentation + 3+ backtick/tilde marker on its own line.

**Risk level**: Low — scanner replaces lazy regex with equivalent but more correct line-by-line processing. All 29 existing tests pass unchanged. No config, protocol, API, or SDK surface changes.

**Merge risk declaration**: No merge risk. Pure additive guard in a single plugin's Memory Wiki markdown extractor. Does not touch lockfile, changelog, or any other bundled plugin.

## ClawSweeper Feedback Addressed (V6)

| Review | Issue | Resolution |
|--------|-------|------------|
| 2026-07-01 P1 | Rebase onto main + narrow diff | Rebased; diff now focused on scanner + export only |
| 2026-07-01 P1 | Replace regex with scanner | Line-by-line scanner handles tilde, longer close, invalid interior fence lines |
| 2026-07-01 P1 | Add redacted wiki lint proof | L2 evidence: 5 real function-call scenarios via `npx tsx` |
| 2026-07-01 P2 | Keep scanning past invalid fence lines (markdown.ts:124) | Scanner continues past any number of invalid close candidates |

## Design Decisions

**Why a line scanner instead of regex?** A regex with lazy quantifier always stops at the first close candidate. When invalid, the engine restarts from past it — leaving the real opening fence unclosed and content after the invalid line unmasked. A scanner checks each candidate line until a valid close is found.

**Why not strip indented (4-space) code blocks?** They overlap with lists/blockquotes. Stripping would risk false-positive removal of real wikilinks.

## Linked context

| Issue/PR | Status | Relationship |
|----------|--------|-------------|
| #97945 | Open | Canonical tracker — this PR targets it directly |
| #97954 | Merged to main | Basic backtick-fence fix via backreference (`\2`) |
| #70986 | Closed (stale) | Original report, validated fix (warnings 70→4) |
